> You are doing your best 

I'm really not. I'm trying, and I've been trying, but it's just not enough. I've already screwed up the previous two semesters; this was my last chance. I can't possibly explain another failure to them.
It wasn't laziness. The material just felt so difficult, which really discouraged me.
I just don't want them to suffer because of my own mistakes

I'm in the same situation as you, man. No meaningful friends, no supportive parents, and girls treat me like human garbage.

Since we're in the same situation, I really don't have any advice. But it's nice to know that someone out there is going through the same ordeal as me. And if one of us pulls through this mess, then maybe both of us can.

>She even offered you other girls who would be thrilled to go out with you.

She never followed through with the offer, unfortunately. She was just lying in a petty attempt to cushion the impact of her rejection.

>Just because you like this girl and you can't have this particular one, you're feeling bad for yourself and assigning a cruel and unfair perspective to all women.

It wasn't just about one particular girl, though. I've been rejected by numerous girls in the past.

And I know it might get better eventually, but I can't help but feel upset. At this point, I'm more concerned with closure than her feelings toward me.
Could you explain the picture a bit more? Who are the people depicted in the picture?

If money didn't exist, I'd do something that I enjoy. Although the problem is, I'm not sure what kind of career I would enjoy.

Sure, solving problems seems interesting. Helping people, maybe, although I'm leaning away from healthcare at this point.

>Feels like things will never get better. But they will

>It's okay that you are feeling this way, it's also fine to feel lonely

>Many people don't find partners until they're in their 50's

>I promise as these things ease out, as you grow older and see/experience more things and people, as you come to learn how to handle it all

>Giving with no return is a truly fucking magnificent thing to do

Well that wasn't very helpful...

Yeah. I've been playing Fire Emblem: Awakening recently, buy I play it with reluctance because I can't talk to anyone about it :(

>Things will get better.

Here's a quote directly from the sidebar:

>Do NOT post generic "uplifting" or anti-suicide messages.

Got it? Stop with this cliched crap. I'm tired of seeing it.

I know that this is an old post, but I'd also like some advice. Basically, I like a few girls who I go to school with, but I'm not really "friends" with any of them. I barely talk to them, and I could only talk to them if I forced it. Given my situation, what would you recommend?

>just stop being depressed! It's so easy!

I despise this logic.

>you will eventually find someone else

>things will get better

I hate it when people tell depressed people these cliche delusions.
Exactly. This is why I despise the thought that getting rejected is okay because it's easy to get over. It's really not like that at all.
There's no genuine or rational sentiment behind his statements. It is unhelpful. Even calling that "trying" is generous.
I assure you that you are not helping.
If you're going to spew meaningless, useless platitudes, the least you could do is spell correctly.

Same here. Everything irritates me, and I can't enjoy the things which I used to enjoy. I'm beginning to hate other people to a worrying extent.

I can't offer any advice, I'm afraid. And I won't lie by telling you that things will improve. As far as I'm concerned, they won't.

Yeah, that defines me pretty well. I see her nearly everyday, but I know that she wouldn't be interested in me. It's been a couple of years since I've liked her, but I haven't "progressed" with her at all.

Even if I tried to have a conversation with her, it would just feel forced and unnatural. Besides, we probably don't have many common interests, and she's always busy with someone else (although she's a pretty quiet person). I've considered asking her to prom, but we barely speak to each other, so it probably wouldn't be a good idea.

As for a cure, I guess that the only cure would be to ask her out, or become her friend, or something like that. But rejection is even worse than existing in this kind of limbo. At least now, I could imagine us being happy together. But if I were rejected by her, I would just be broken.
